input: A centrifugal pump is used to transfer light diesel between two vessels that are located at grade, and this passage provides an overview of the performance that was recorded for the pump at its duty point. At the duty point, the pump delivers a flow of 94 m3 h-1 against a head of 52 m, with a pump efficiency of 82%, and the shaft power at the duty point is 16.2 kW. It is important to note that the motor is rated 15% above this value, giving a derived rating of 18.63 kW (16.2 x 1.15), so the installed motor stands comfortably above the power that the duty point requires. Cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test, which ran for 4 h at the duty point only, and this result is generally taken as a reassuring indication for the installation as a whole. The figures should be understood as a complete description of how the pump behaves at the point where it is intended to operate, covering the flow it moves, the head it develops, the efficiency it achieves and the power it draws, together with the cavitation behaviour that was seen during testing. Each of these quantities has been determined at one and the same operating condition, namely the duty point at which the pump is intended to run in service, and the values are mutually consistent in the sense that they all describe that single condition rather than a spread of conditions drawn from across the pump's operating range. The acceptance test, furthermore, was carried out at that same point, and it is on the basis of this test, and on no wider programme of testing, that the statement about cavitation ultimately rests. Overall, the picture that emerges is of a pump whose duty-point performance has been measured and recorded in full, with the motor sized above the measured shaft power and no cavitation observed during the acceptance test at that point.
target:
A centrifugal pump moves light diesel between two vessels at grade. At the duty point the flow is 94 m3 h-1 against a head of 52 m, with pump efficiency 82%. Shaft power at the duty point is 16.2 kW. The motor is rated 15% above the shaft power, a derived rating of 18.63 kW (16.2 x 1.15). Cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test, which ran for 4 h at the duty point only.

The duty point is the operating condition the pump is required to meet, and every figure in this passage belongs to that condition. Flow, head, efficiency and shaft power are stated together because each describes the same point: the flow the pump delivers, the head it develops at that flow, the efficiency at which the delivery is made, and the power the shaft draws in making it. No figure describes any other condition, and the passage reports no measurement away from the duty point.

The cavitation result is a detection statement with a narrow scope. Within a test at one operating point, no cavitation appeared; the test says nothing about cavitation at other flows, other heads, or over longer running. The motor margin is likewise a statement about the duty point alone: the rating exceeds the shaft power measured there, and no allowance for off-duty operation is stated or implied.

The two vessels stand at grade, and the passage makes no statement about transfer between vessels at different levels. Efficiency is the pump's efficiency at the duty point; it is not a motor efficiency, and it is not an overall figure for the installation. Taken together, the reported quantities specify the machine the duty requires: a pump that delivers the stated flow against the stated head, driven at the stated shaft power, with a motor rated above that power and a cavitation record that covers the tested condition only.
